body: @bebraw thank you! I'm not sure if it is a question or a feature request.

Thank you for the configuration. I realized that my description wasn't clear... 

I've put together a [test repo](https://github.com/kmalakoff/webpack-test) to show the problem.

If you compare webpack to node, you'll see they behave differently:

Node.js

```
$ node entry.js

Module1: pre-require
Module1: post-require (error)
Module1: post-require (finally)
Module2: pre-require
Module2: post-require (error)
Module2: post-require (finally)
```

```
$ webpack
$ open index.html

(console)
Module1: pre-require
Module1: post-require (error)
Module1: post-require (finally)
Module2: pre-require
Module2: async undefined
Module2: post-require (finally)
```

Basically, node throws each time the module is required, but webpack only throws the first time.

The use case I had was where multiple libraries used require('fsevents') to feature detect whether fsevents was available inside a try / catch block. The first library caught the exception which changed the program flow, but the second library received an empty object from webpack so their try / catch logic for fallback wasn't triggered.

This might be an edge-case where webpack doesn't need to be identical to node. I just ran into the discrepancy so filed the "bug" / "feature".

Thank you for webpack!
webpack should behave identical to node.js here.

This requires a try-catch block in the webpack runtime. This would have big performance implications...

As nobody noticed it for year, we could be incompatible to node.js here, for performance reasons.

The performance, feature parity, and "hasn't been a problem for anyone so far" arguments all make sense.

I've found a work around by forking one of the libraries so not a problem for me anymore so I'll leave it in your hands to discuss and decide. Thank you!
Ok we discuss it and will add a opt-in option to enable correct behavior for exceptions while module loading.
Sounds like a good balance. Thank you!
